lines: OpenAI's Ari Weinstein and James Sun argue computer-using agents now work faster than the average human, and that the next step — superhuman speed — will change how people interact with software.

They frame the screen itself as a universal interface: agents can automate legacy enterprise systems that never got APIs, with standards like WebMCP helping agents and humans share the same interfaces.
They say cutting 'thinking tokens' drives both speed and reliability for OpenAI's Astra model, and that small gains — say from 97% to 99% task success — matter a lot for enterprise trust.

Enterprise adoption, in their view, needs deterministic sandbox controls plus configurable human-in-the-loop review, while the best workflows shift toward proactive background agents that fix issues before people notice.
They expect traditional UIs to survive because people like direct manipulation, and see the startup opportunity in vertical tools that stitch together non-API legacy systems.
title: OpenAI: When AI Agents Use Computers Faster Than You
